findings.title: Application data manually re-keyed from forms into the loan origination system
findings.root: Intake channel is not integrated with the LOS; the form is a PDF or web form exported to an advisor.
findings.symptom: Typos propagate downstream; every downstream check inherits bad data; ~15–30 min of pure typing per file.

findings.title: No completeness gate at submission — incomplete files enter the pipeline
findings.root: The procedure lists required documents but nothing validates them at the point of entry.
findings.symptom: Rework loops: the file bounces between customer, advisor and case manager 2–4 times.

findings.title: Channel fragmentation — branch, broker and online capture data in different formats
findings.root: Each channel was digitized separately; no canonical application data model.
findings.symptom: Same field means different things per channel; reporting and downstream rules break silently.

findings.title: Documents collected over email with no structured tracking of what is missing
findings.root: Email is the system of record for documents; the checklist lives in someone's head or a spreadsheet.
findings.symptom: Files stall for days waiting on a document nobody chased; no visibility of aging per document.

findings.title: Manual classification and indexing of incoming documents
findings.root: Staff read each attachment and decide what it is and where it goes in the DMS.
findings.symptom: Misfiled documents surface weeks later at underwriting; indexing consumes analyst time.

findings.title: Key data extracted manually from payslips, bank statements and tax forms
findings.root: No OCR/extraction pipeline; numbers are read off PDFs and typed into assessment tools.
findings.symptom: Transcription errors directly hit affordability; extraction is the single biggest time sink in file preparation.

findings.title: No automated authenticity or fraud screening of submitted documents
findings.root: Visual inspection only; manipulated PDFs and forged payslips pass unless an analyst happens to spot them.
findings.symptom: Fraud discovered post-disbursement or never; loss events are treated as bad luck rather than a control gap.

findings.title: Existing customers re-verified from scratch instead of reusing KYC records
findings.root: KYC records are product-siloed; the mortgage process cannot see the retail KYC file.
findings.symptom: Customers resubmit documents the bank already holds; duplicated analyst effort; worse experience for loyal customers.

findings.title: Sanctions/PEP screening is a swivel-chair step in a separate tool
findings.root: Screening tool is not embedded in the workflow; results are copy-pasted or attached as screenshots.
findings.symptom: Screening evidence is not linked to the case; timing of the check vs. decision is not provable.

findings.title: Weak audit trail of who verified what and when
findings.root: Verification steps are recorded as free-text notes or not recorded at all.
findings.symptom: Regulator or internal audit requests trigger manual archaeology across mailboxes and folders.

findings.title: Income verified via employer calls, letters or manual document review
findings.root: No open-banking or payroll data integration; income confirmation depends on third-party responsiveness.
findings.symptom: Multi-day delays; unverifiable income leads to conservative declines or manual exceptions.

findings.title: Affordability model inputs keyed manually into calculators/spreadsheets
findings.root: The affordability model lives outside the LOS as a spreadsheet or standalone calculator.
findings.symptom: Input errors distort DTI/LTV; spreadsheet versions diverge between teams and over time.

findings.title: Bureau data pulled manually and stored as PDFs
findings.root: Bureau access is via a web portal, not an API wired into the decision flow.
findings.symptom: Stale reports reused; structured bureau attributes unavailable to scoring; refresh discipline depends on the analyst.

findings.title: Credit policy rules hardcoded — changes require an IT release
findings.root: Policy is embedded in code or in the LOS configuration, owned by IT rather than risk.
findings.symptom: Weeks-to-months lag between a policy decision and its enforcement; workarounds and shadow spreadsheets appear.

findings.title: Valuation ordering, chasing and receipt handled by phone and email
findings.root: No integration with valuation providers or panel managers; status is tracked manually.
findings.symptom: Valuation is the longest pole in most files; nobody can answer 'where is my valuation' without phone calls.

findings.title: No automated cross-check of valuation against market data
findings.root: Valuations accepted at face value; AVM/statistical cross-checks not used even as a second opinion.
findings.symptom: Outlier valuations pass unnoticed; collateral risk discovered at audit or default.

findings.title: Collateral data re-keyed into the core banking system
findings.root: Collateral registration is a separate manual step after the decision.
findings.symptom: Mismatches between the LOS and core banking collateral records; registration delays extend time-to-money.

findings.title: Underwriters spend most of their time assembling the file, not deciding
findings.root: Case summary, data gathering and cross-checking are manual; the decision itself is the minority of effort.
findings.symptom: Scarce expert capacity burned on clerical work; queue times grow with volume, not complexity.

findings.title: Exceptions handled in email threads with no case ownership or SLA
findings.root: The procedure defines the happy path; deviations escape into unstructured communication.
findings.symptom: Exception files age invisibly; decisions depend on who is copied; institutional memory is lost when people leave.

findings.title: Decision rationale captured inconsistently — audit and model-risk exposure
findings.root: Rationale is free text, quality varies by underwriter; overrides poorly documented.
findings.symptom: Hard to evidence why a loan was approved; problematic for regulators, internal audit and model validation.

findings.title: Approval conditions tracked manually — files stall waiting for conditions
findings.root: Conditions live in the decision letter; no workflow engine tracks their fulfilment.
findings.symptom: Approved files die on the vine; conversion from approval to disbursement leaks without anyone owning it.

findings.title: Offer letters generated manually or via fragile mail-merge
findings.root: Document generation is not data-driven from the LOS; terms are typed or merged manually.
findings.symptom: Wrong terms in offers; legal review loops; version confusion between drafts.

findings.title: Signing requires a physical branch visit — no e-signature path
findings.root: Wet-ink process by default, even where e-signature is legally available.
findings.symptom: Days lost to scheduling; drop-off at the last mile; poor experience for remote customers.

findings.title: Disbursement checklist executed manually across multiple teams
findings.root: Payout requires coordinated checks (insurance, registration, conditions) with no orchestration.
findings.symptom: Time-to-money varies wildly; files ping-pong between legal, back office and treasury.

findings.title: Context lost at handover to servicing — data re-onboarded
findings.root: Origination and servicing run on separate systems with a thin data bridge.
findings.symptom: Servicing re-verifies data the bank already validated; early-warning signals from origination are lost.

findings.title: No proactive monitoring triggers seeded at origination
findings.root: Risk flags known at origination (e.g. variable income, high LTV) are not converted into monitoring rules.
findings.symptom: Early delinquency signals missed; collections is surprised by risks underwriting already saw.

findings.title: Customer communication is reactive — high call-centre load for status questions
findings.root: No proactive status updates; customers call to find out where their file is.
findings.symptom: Call volume spikes correlate with pipeline congestion; satisfaction drops at exactly the moments of delay.

solutions.name: Document Intelligence Agent
solutions.desc: An agent that owns the document lifecycle: requests missing items from the customer, classifies and indexes what arrives, extracts structured data (income, identity, liabilities) with OCR + LLM extraction, runs authenticity and fraud screening, and maintains a live completeness checklist per file.
solutions.hitl: Analysts review low-confidence extractions and fraud flags; nothing is silently auto-accepted into the credit file.
solutions.architecture: Document intake API -> classification model -> extraction with confidence scoring -> validation against LOS data -> DMS write-back with full provenance log.
solutions.kpis: Document cycle time, extraction accuracy, rework loop count, fraud catch rate.

solutions.name: Smart Intake & Orchestration Agent
solutions.desc: A conversational intake layer (web/branch/broker) that guides the applicant, validates entries in real time against a canonical data model, pre-fills known customer data, and writes straight through to the LOS — no re-keying.
solutions.hitl: Advisors handle exceptions the agent cannot resolve; the agent escalates with full context.
solutions.architecture: Canonical application schema + channel adapters + LOS API; the LLM handles dialogue and field mapping, deterministic rules enforce validation.
solutions.kpis: Straight-through rate at intake, data-entry error rate, application completion rate.

solutions.name: KYC / Perpetual-KYC Copilot
solutions.desc: Reuses existing KYC records across products, triggers delta-verification only where data is stale, embeds sanctions/PEP screening in the workflow, and writes a structured, timestamped evidence trail for every check.
solutions.hitl: Compliance analysts decide on hits and enhanced due diligence; the copilot prepares the evidence package.
solutions.architecture: KYC record graph + screening API integration + evidence store with immutable audit log.
solutions.kpis: KYC reuse rate, screening cycle time, audit-evidence completeness.

solutions.name: Income & Affordability Verification Agent
solutions.desc: Verifies income through open banking / payroll APIs where consented, falls back to document intelligence where not; feeds a governed affordability engine; moves credit policy into a decision layer the risk team controls without IT releases.
solutions.hitl: Credit analysts review borderline affordability and unverifiable income cases.
solutions.architecture: Open-banking aggregation + transaction categorisation model + policy-as-code decision service with versioning.
solutions.kpis: Income verification time, affordability input error rate, policy change lead time.

solutions.name: Valuation Orchestration + AVM Cross-Check
solutions.desc: Automates valuation ordering, status tracking and chasing with providers; runs an automated valuation model as a statistical second opinion; syncs collateral data to core banking without re-keying.
solutions.hitl: Collateral team reviews files where AVM and manual valuation diverge beyond tolerance.
solutions.architecture: Provider APIs / panel manager integration + AVM service + collateral data sync.
solutions.kpis: Valuation turnaround, outlier catch rate, collateral data mismatches.

solutions.name: Underwriting Copilot (human-in-the-loop)
solutions.desc: Assembles the complete case automatically: structured summary of the file, extracted evidence with source links, policy compliance pre-check, draft decision rationale, and conditions tracked as workflow objects with owners and deadlines. The underwriter decides — the copilot does everything around the decision.
solutions.hitl: The credit decision remains human (required for regulated credit in most jurisdictions); the copilot recommends and documents, never auto-decides borderline cases.
solutions.architecture: Case assembly agent + retrieval over the credit file + policy engine pre-check + rationale drafting with citation-to-source + conditions workflow.
solutions.kpis: Underwriter time per file, decision rationale quality score, condition fulfilment rate, approval-to-disbursement conversion.

solutions.name: Offer Generation & Disbursement Orchestration
solutions.desc: Generates offer documents data-driven from the LOS with legal-approved templates, routes signing through e-signature, and orchestrates the disbursement checklist across legal, back office and treasury with a visible state machine.
solutions.hitl: Legal reviews template deviations; back office confirms payout conditions the system cannot verify.
solutions.architecture: Template engine bound to LOS data + e-signature integration + disbursement workflow orchestrator.
solutions.kpis: Offer error rate, time from approval to signature, time-to-money variance.

solutions.name: Servicing Handover & Monitoring Agent
solutions.desc: Carries the full origination context into servicing, converts origination risk flags into monitoring triggers, and handles proactive customer communication (status updates, document reminders) across channels.
solutions.hitl: Servicing staff handle hardship and collections conversations; the agent handles information flow.
solutions.architecture: Origination-to-servicing data bridge + rules/triggers seeded from underwriting + proactive notification service.
solutions.kpis: Status-call volume, early-delinquency detection lead time, servicing data rework.
